transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, to be perfectly honest with you, I wouldn't even be here if it wasn't for my work physical. You see, the company requires us to get checked out every year, just to make sure we're fit for the job, which makes sense, I guess, since being a mechanic is pretty physical work. You're always bending, lifting, squeezing into tight spaces under cars. Anyway, the doctor who did the physical, he got all worked up because he said my weight is too low. He started throwing around all these numbers and charts, acting like it was some big emergency. But honestly? I don't get what the fuss is about. I feel great. Better than great, actually. I play in a men's basketball league on Tuesday nights, and since I dropped some weight, I feel so much lighter on my feet. I'm moving faster, getting up and down the court easier. And even at the garage, I don't feel as weighed down when I'm working a long shift. I used to get so sluggish by the afternoon, but now I just feel... streamlined, you know? So, I'm just here because they told me I had to follow up, but I really think that work doctor was just overreacting to a number on a scale instead of looking at how I'm actually doing.
Have you intentionally lost weight, or has the weight loss happened without you specifically trying to lose weight?

Well, "intentional" is kind of a funny word for it, honestly. It's not like I'm sitting there with a calculator adding up points or joining some trendy weight loss group, you know? It's more about... efficiency, I guess you could say. 

You see, the shop is just non-stop right now. We've been short-staffed for months, so I'm pulling extra tickets, and the bays are always full. It's loud, it's hot, and you're constantly on your feet. And then by the time I finally clock out and get home, the house is just a total madhouse. Everyone's going in ten different directions, there's always something that needs fixing or paying attention to, and it's just a lot of chaos. 

So, somewhere along the line, I just started simplifying things for myself to cut through all that noise. I found that I just function better if I don't bog myself down. Most days, I keep it to just coffee in the morning—gets the engine running, you know? And then I don't really mess with a big lunch because it just makes me want to take a nap under a Chevy. I'll maybe have a small sandwich, or if the guys order out or there's food at home, I'll just eat half of whatever is around later in the day. 

It’s just easier that way. With the shop running late all the time and the house being so busy, I just feel better sticking to my own simple rules. It gives me a little bit of order. I don't have to think about it, I just follow my routine, keep it light, and keep moving. So, did I specifically *try* to lose the weight? I mean, I guess the weight coming off was just a byproduct of me finally getting my day under control and sticking to my system. It just works better for me.
Do you ever feel distressed or concerned about your eating habits or the fact that you've lost weight?

Distressed? No, no, I wouldn't say distressed at all. Honestly, it's kind of the opposite. I feel like I've finally got a handle on things. But, you know, it's funny you ask that, because my wife—she's been getting on my case about it lately. She'll say things like, "You're wasting away," or "You need to eat a real meal," especially when we're sitting down with the kids and I'm just having my half-portion or whatever. And the guys at the shop, they've made a few comments too, usually when they're stuffing their faces with greasy pizza and I'm just having my coffee. They'll joke that a strong gust of wind is going to blow me away while I'm out in the lot. 

So, I know people are worried, or at least they act like they are. But I figure they’re making way too much of it. I mean, look at the facts, right? If I was really in some kind of trouble, if this was actually a problem, wouldn't I be falling apart? But I'm not. I still show up for work every single day, usually early, and I pull my weight in the garage just fine. I still take care of what needs doing at home—mowing the lawn, fixing the leaky sink, running the kids to their activities. And like I said, I still play ball on weekends. You can't run a full court for an hour if you're sick, you know? 

So, when they get all concerned, or when that work doctor started waving his charts around, I just kind of brush it off. It feels like everyone else is distressed about it, but me? I'm just living my life, getting things done, and honestly doing it better than I was before. I just don't see the big deal when everything is running smoothly, you know? It's like bringing a car in for a major engine overhaul when it's purring like a kitten. Why fix what isn't broken?
Have you ever felt that your weight loss was beyond your control or not in line with your health goals?

Well, out of my control? No, no, I wouldn't say that at all. In fact, it's the exact opposite, really. I feel like I have more control now than I ever have. But... well, I will admit, there is one thing that gets under my skin a bit. It's not that I feel out of control, it's just... I get really, really bothered if things start going the other direction, you know? 

Like, if I step on the scale in the morning—which I do, you know, just to keep track, just to make sure the system is working—and I see it bump up even a pound or two. Or, say, I pull on my work jeans and they feel just a little bit tighter around the waist than they did the day before. Man, it just... it really messes with my head. I start thinking, "Okay, here we go, I'm getting soft again." And it's not just about how it looks, it's about how it feels. I start worrying that if I let it slide, if I let that weight creep back on, I'm going to lose that edge I was telling you about. 

I picture myself trying to slide under a transmission and getting stuck, or feeling that heavy, sluggish feeling halfway through a double shift. Or on the basketball court—I start thinking I won't be able to make those fast breaks, that I'll be huffing and puffing while the younger guys run right past me. It's like, I've worked so hard to get this machine running lean and mean, and the thought of putting junk back in the trunk, so to speak, it just really... it freaks me out a little bit. So, yeah, I guess I do get pretty intense about making sure the weight doesn't come back, because I just don't want to go back to feeling slow and weighed down.

latest_inference.note: The patient's preoccupation with weight gain, rigid eating behaviors, and significant weight loss despite normal physiological functioning are indicative of Anorexia Nervosa. Other differential diagnoses (e.g., depression, malnutrition due to medical causes) are less consistent with the patient's presentation and have been ruled out based on the clinical interview.
